name: Kurigram
tagline: Sixteen rivers, a hundred chars, and the home of Bhawaiya — Bangladesh's far north-west corner.

guide.bestTime: November to February (cool, dry; the chars accessible and the Dharla calm)
guide.gettingThere: By train to Kurigram station on the northern line, or by road from Dhaka (~8 hr) and Rangpur (~1.5 hr). No airport — the nearest is Saidpur (Nilphamari), ~75 km away.
guide.difficulty: Easy in town and the Sadar belt; char (river-island) and Roumari trips are moderate and need dry-season timing.

mustVisit.name: Ulipur Munshibari
mustVisit.description: The decaying 18th-century estate of the Munshi family at Dharanibari in Ulipur — a domed administrative house with playhouse, barnyard, Durga and Vishnu temples, dining hall and kitchen, all still legible amid the ruin.
mustVisit.history: Founded in the mid-18th century during the reign of Nawab Sirajuddaula by a Mughal-era official, the estate served as the seat of a feudal lineage that gave the locality its name. The compound is now a protected antiquity under the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh.

practical.hours: Daylight (exterior only — the interior is structurally unsafe)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 22 km south-east of Kurigram town in Dharanibari union, Ulipur Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Ulipur, then easybike to Dharanibari

tips: Do not climb the upper floors — the masonry is failing
Pair with the Bhawaiya Academy at Ulipur for a cultural half-day

mustVisit.name: Chandamari Mosque (Rajarhat)
mustVisit.description: A small three-domed Mughal-era brick mosque at Mandalpara in Rajarhat — one of the oldest standing mosques in Rangpur division.
mustVisit.history: Believed to have been built between the late 16th and late 17th centuries during Mughal rule in Bengal, the mosque follows the classic three-dome plan with Islamic geometric ornament. It is listed under the Department of Archaeology.

practical.hours: Open during five daily prayers; visitors welcome outside prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Mandalpara, Rajarhat Upazila, ~15 km west of Kurigram town
howToReach.transport: CNG or bus to Rajarhat, then easybike to Mandalpara

mustVisit.bestTime: Outside Friday noon prayers; morning light
tips: Cover head if female; remove shoes before entering
The interior is small — the carved façade is the highlight

mustVisit.name: Bhitorbond Zamindar Bari (Nageshwari)
mustVisit.description: An old zamindari mansion in Nageshwari that once served as the administrative seat of the Bhitorbond Pargana — a quiet, atmospheric ruin.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 16 km north of Kurigram town in Nageshwari Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Nageshwari, then easybike

tips: Little is signposted — ask in Nageshwari bazar for directions
Combine with a stop at the Dudhkumar riverbank nearby

mustVisit.name: Dharla Bridge & Riverfront
mustVisit.description: The 950-metre Dharla Bridge and the riverbank just outside Kurigram town — a popular sunset spot with grilled-corn stalls and easy access to the river.
mustVisit.history: The 2nd Dharla Bridge, 950 m long and 9.80 m wide, has 19 spans and is the headline crossing on the road north out of Kurigram town.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On the northern edge of Kurigram town, on the Dharla

tips: Walk down to the embankment for the wider view
Roadside stalls grill maize and serve sweet tea in the evenings

mustVisit.name: Chilmari River Port & Brahmaputra Chars
mustVisit.description: The Brahmaputra river port at Chilmari and the chain of chars (river-islands) stretching out beyond it — a stark, wide-water landscape of sandbar farms and ferry boats.
mustVisit.history: Chilmari has been a river port since the colonial period, once a major trading point on the Brahmaputra. The chars beyond it are dry-season homes to communities who farm maize, chili, groundnut and watermelon in the sandy soil.

practical.hours: Daylight; go and return well before dark

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 35 km south-east of Kurigram town in Chilmari Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus or CNG to Chilmari, then country boat from the port

mustVisit.bestTime: Dry season (Nov–Mar); avoid monsoon flood months
tips: Go with a local boatman who knows the current year's channels
Carry water and sun cover — there is no shade on the sandbars

mustVisit.name: Bhawaiya Academy, Ulipur
mustVisit.description: A modest tin-roofed academy in Ulipur that has been preserving and teaching Bhawaiya — the soulful folk music of the northern delta — for over three decades.
mustVisit.history: Founded in 1994 when a former Durgapur union chairman, Golep Uddin Sarkar, donated five decimals of land, the academy has become the working heart of Bhawaiya in Bangladesh — running classes, gatherings and a small museum of folk instruments and recordings.

practical.hours: Best to call ahead — performances are seasonal

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Ulipur Upazila, ~22 km south-east of Kurigram town

tips: Ask about a small recital — the elongated, mournful Bhawaiya tones repay a slow listen
Pair with Ulipur Munshibari in the same upazila

specialties.name: Bhawaiya Folk Music
specialties.description: The signature folk tradition of greater Rangpur — Cooch Behar — Goalpara, with its long-drawn tones and themes of mahouts, mahishals and gariyals (cart drivers). Kurigram is one of its living centres.
specialties.timing: Winter season; festivals and academy recitals

specialties.name: Char Maize, Chili & Groundnut
specialties.description: The chars of the Brahmaputra, Dharla and Teesta grow maize (bhutta), red chili and groundnut in the sandy soil — sold grilled at the ghats and dried at the rural haats.
specialties.venue: Chilmari, Roumari, Char Rajibpur ghats & haats

specialties.name: Aakher Gur (Sugarcane Molasses)
specialties.description: Northern Bengal's gur of choice — sugarcane molasses pressed and boiled at village mills, used in winter pithas and tea.

specialties.name: Char Watermelon
specialties.description: A newer success story — watermelons grown in the sandy char soil of the Brahmaputra, transforming dry-season livelihoods in Chilmari and Roumari.

bucketlist.title: Hear a Bhawaiya song at the Ulipur academy
bucketlist.detail: The elongated, mournful folk music of the cart-drivers and mahishals of the northern delta — kept alive at a tin-roofed academy founded in 1994.

bucketlist.title: Explore the ruined Ulipur Munshibari
bucketlist.detail: An 18th-century domed estate founded in Nawab Sirajuddaula's reign — playhouse, barnyard, temples and kitchens, all still legible in the ruin.

bucketlist.title: Visit the three-domed Chandamari Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A small Mughal-era mosque at Mandalpara — one of the oldest standing mosques in Rangpur division.

bucketlist.title: Watch sunset over the Dharla Bridge
bucketlist.detail: The 950-metre, 19-span bridge frames the river at golden hour; embankment stalls grill corn as the evening rolls in.

bucketlist.title: Take a boat from Chilmari into the Brahmaputra chars
bucketlist.detail: Step onto a sandbar island of maize, chili and watermelon and meet the communities who farm between the floods.

bucketlist.title: Find the Bhitorbond zamindar bari at Nageshwari
bucketlist.detail: The old administrative seat of the Bhitorbond Pargana — a quiet ruin in the district's north.

bucketlist.title: Eat char-grown watermelon in spring
bucketlist.detail: A new lifeline crop on the Brahmaputra sandbars — bright, sweet melons from the dry-season chars.

bucketlist.title: Snack on grilled char maize at a riverbank stall
bucketlist.detail: Corn from the chars, charred on the cob over coals — the simplest, best taste of the northern rivers.

bucketlist.title: Buy fresh aakher gur at a winter haat
bucketlist.detail: Northern Bengal's sugarcane molasses, pressed and boiled at village mills — the base of pithas and tea.

bucketlist.title: Read Syed Shamsul Haq on home ground
bucketlist.detail: The 'sabyasachi' poet, novelist and playwright behind 'Payer Awaj Paowa Jay' was born here in 1935. His rivers and town shape the landscape around you.

bucketlist.title: Visit a quieter riverbank on the Dudhkumar
bucketlist.detail: Beyond the Dharla and Brahmaputra, the smaller Dudhkumar runs through Nageshwari — fewer visitors, the same wide light.

bucketlist.title: Eat winter pitha with aakher gur
bucketlist.detail: Chitoi and bhapa rice cakes with northern sugarcane gur, served at winter-morning stalls in the upazila bazaars.

foods.name: Char Maize (Bhutta)
foods.description: Corn grown on the chars of the Brahmaputra, Dharla and Teesta — grilled on the cob at the riverside ghats.

foods.name: Char Watermelon
foods.description: Sweet melons from the sandy char soil of the Brahmaputra — a newer dry-season crop with a famously bright juice.

foods.name: Char Groundnut & Red Chili
foods.description: Peanuts roasted warm at the ghats, and the fiery dried red chili of the chars.

foods.name: Aakher Gur
foods.description: Sugarcane molasses pressed and boiled at village mills — the northern alternative to date-palm gur, used in tea and pithas.

foods.name: Aakher Gur Pitha
foods.description: Winter rice pithas — chitoi and bhapa — drizzled with hot sugarcane molasses.

foods.name: Sidol / Shutki Bhorta
foods.description: Pungent north-Bengal fermented and dried-fish mash, pounded with chili and onion — a regional staple.

foods.name: Brahmaputra & Dharla River Fish
foods.description: Fresh catch from the big rivers — carp, catfish and small char-river fish in light mustard curries.

famousPeople.name: Syed Shamsul Haq
famousPeople.knownFor: 'Sabyasachi' writer — poet, novelist, dramatist and translator across nearly every Bengali form. Born in Kurigram on 27 December 1935; author of 'Payer Awaj Paowa Jay', the canonical Liberation War drama. Honoured with the Bangla Academy Award, the Adamjee Award and the Ekushey Padak.

didYouKnow: Kurigram became a district on 1 February 1984, carved out of greater Rangpur — its nine upazilas include the far-eastern chars of Roumari and Char Rajibpur.
The district sits at the confluence of the Brahmaputra, Dharla and Teesta, with a constellation of smaller rivers (Dudhkumar, Phulkumar) and dozens of seasonal chars.
Bhawaiya, the long-toned folk music of the northern delta, is at home here — taught and kept alive at the Bhawaiya Academy at Ulipur since 1994.
Ulipur Munshibari was founded in the mid-18th century during the reign of Nawab Sirajuddaula and is now a protected antiquity.
Chandamari Mosque in Rajarhat was built during Mughal rule (late 16th–17th century) — one of the oldest standing mosques in Rangpur division.
